materials.name: Graphene Lattice
materials.desc: Single-atom carbon sheeting made from biomass. Used as reinforcement and a conductor in higher-tier systems.

materials.name: Graphene Lattice (Carbide Route)
materials.desc: Single-atom carbon sheeting made by reducing hull alloys instead of biomass. Higher yield and alloy cost; useful where nothing grows.

materials.name: Boron Nitride Ceramic
materials.desc: Hexagonal boron nitride. Insulates against current and transfers heat from drill faces and reactor walls.

materials.name: Deuterium Slush
materials.desc: Heavy hydrogen distilled from the metallic phase and chilled into a pumpable slurry. Fusion fuel; leaves tritium as a byproduct.

materials.name: Silica Aerogel
materials.desc: Silica foam that is over 99% void by volume. Used for thermal insulation and low-mass structural filler.

materials.name: Silica Aerogel (Vacuum Route)
materials.desc: Aerogel dried in open vacuum instead of heat. Higher yield and lower alloy cost, with an exotic-matter cost.

materials.name: Tritium Residue
materials.desc: Radioactive hydrogen isotope left after deuterium distillation. Decays continuously and must be captured in a getter bed.

materials.name: High-Entropy Alloy Billet
materials.desc: Five principal elements in a solid solution with high fatigue resistance. Structural stock for high-load frames.

materials.name: YBCO Tape
materials.desc: Yttrium barium copper oxide on metal tape. Superconducts above liquid-nitrogen temperature for magnet windings and power runs.

materials.name: Metamaterial Film
materials.desc: Sub-wavelength lattice with a negative refractive index. Bends light backward for sensor optics and signal masking.

materials.name: Bose-Einstein Condensate Cell
materials.desc: A few million atoms held near absolute zero in one quantum state. Timing and inertial reference for precision instruments.

materials.name: Tritium Getter Bed
materials.desc: Heated metal bed that absorbs tritium into a stable hydride. Stores the residue from deuterium distillation as fuel.

materials.name: Casimir Plate Stack
materials.desc: Conductive plates held nanometres apart. Vacuum fluctuation pressure forces them together and produces usable force.

materials.name: Penning Positron Trap
materials.desc: Crossed magnetic and electrostatic fields confine positrons away from the chamber walls. Stores antimatter for power and cutting tools.

materials.name: Degenerate Matter Core
materials.desc: Compressed neutron-star matter held by electron degeneracy pressure. Used for dense ballast and inertial masses.

materials.name: Muon-Catalysed Fusion Cell
materials.desc: Muons replace electrons in deuterium-tritium molecules and catalyse fusion at ambient temperature. Each lasts about two microseconds and drives several hundred reactions.

materials.name: Viable Gene Line
materials.desc: A preserved human genetic line returned from a colony clinic.

materials.name: Statite Mirror
materials.desc: Field hardware that holds a mirror against a star's gravity.

materials.name: Thermophotovoltaic Film
materials.desc: Converts waste light from a star into power for a Dyson swarm.

materials.name: Momentum Tether
materials.desc: Alien inertial coupling for carrying a swarm's orbital loads.

materials.name: Self-Replicating Probe
materials.desc: Warp-equipped census probe built by humanity. Its purpose is up to us.
